reduction: Substitutionx=c+p gives the exact Pick quarticF=B-4*c*(c+p)*H. All data feasible withc>0 are exactly(p,y)inD andc>=psi(p,y), with the one zero-threshold pointp=0,y=1 allowingeveryc>0.
Dforcesy>0. B>=0 with equality only atp=0,y=1. Away fromthatpoint,B/H>0 impliespsi>max(0,-p), sox=c+p>0 is automatic; no wrong-sign branch is lost.
Atp=0,y=1,psi=0, and anyconstantf=c+i is feasible. The closed epigraph includesc=0 there, corresponding only toboundaryconstantf=i. The original openquadrant family excludes thatvertex.
H=0 cannot hold at a feasible finitec: B>0 ontheboundaryofD forr>0. As(p,y)approachesthatboundary,psi diverges. No division byHzero or compactness of thefullunboundedbody is assumed.

The fullclosedbody is a convex epigraph in(c,p,y), because it is the closure of the convex analytic interpolation image after a linear coordinate change. Its only nonzero recession direction ispositive(1,0,0) in(c,p,y), equivalentlypositive(1,1,0) in(c,x,y): D is bounded, and adding a nonnegative realconstanttof preserves feasibility.
two_node_objective: If the residue functional isLambda(f)=gamma*(f(z)-f(0)) (two simple value nodes andLambda(1)=0), thenJ=Im(gamma)*p+Re(gamma)*(y-1)-c. Since the coefficient ofc is-1, eliminatec by takingpsi; the threshold becomes sup_D[Im(gamma)*p+Re(gamma)*(y-1)-psi]. At the zero-threshold vertex this is a supremum approached byc downarrow0, not necessarily an admissible maximizer. This does not assert that every profile has onlythese two value nodes.
hypothesis_reduction: The joint variablec two-node membership problem has an explicit scalar epigraph formula and the normalized variablec can be eliminated from the stated two-residue objective. This is not a jointly affine semidefinite lift or a higher-jet formula.
